newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA SUSPENDS SENTENCE IN BRITON BABY SMUGGLING.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA SUSPENDS SENTENCE IN BRITON BABY SMUGGLING.

text.p: A Romanian court on Monday handed down a suspended 20-month jail sentence to Briton John Boast over charges of smuggling babies out Romania, court sources said.

"I've never thought I could get a sentence for the simple reason of having been seen with some children who eventually turned up in Britain," Boast, dressed in stained overalls told reporters in Romanian.

Boast, 46, a self-described charity worker from Harwood in Lancashire, was first charged more than one year ago with smuggling a 15-month-old Romanian gypsy girl over the border with Hungary to Britain for illegal adoption.

In 1996, he was arrested over a second case -- the purchase for the equivalent of $60 of two-year-old gypsy girl Viola Szilagy, who was taken out of Romania in June 1995. He was eventually freed after six months in police custody.
The court in the Transylvanian city of Oradea, near the border with Hungary, also passed a 18-month suspended jail sentence to Viola's father.
Prosecutor Adina Dumitrescu said she would appeal Monday's court ruling demanding that Boast should be expelled.
"We'll appeal because the court did not take the safety measure of preventing a reiteration of offences and did not order Boast, who is a foreigner, out of the country," she said.
Presiding judge Dumitru Marc said he had not asked for Boast's expulsion because he "enjoys big support among families with many children" in his capacity as charity worker.
Boast had been visiting Romania ferrying truckloads of aid after the 1989 collapse of communism, when reports of abandoned babies living in gruesome orphanages stunned the world.
The centrist government last week passed a decree to stop unscrupulous baby-traders making a profit from foreigners seeking to adopt among Romania's 100,000 abandoned children.
An average of some 2,500 children were legally adopted by foreigners annually since 1989. But aid groups say another 10,000 may have gone illegally.

Boast is the third Briton tried with baby smuggling after the British couple Adrian and Bernadette Mooney had been sentenced to two years and four months in jail for buying and trying to smuggle a baby out of Romania in 1994. Their sentence was pardoned by Romania's President.
"That I was convicted does not matter," Boast said. "What matters to me is that I be allowed to stay in Romania where I have done many good things for the children." REUTER
